Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates a well-defined mass located in the posterior mediastinum, situated behind the heart and causing anterior displacement of the trachea. This location and effect are characteristic of an esophageal lesion, such as a lipoma or leiomyoma, whereas bronchogenic cysts are typically middle mediastinal and lymphomas/thymomas are anterior.
